## p150 A2 — Embassy receiving station listens; encipher addresses and call every period; second part only

**Edition context:** Radio contact, operating times and an unavailable key.

**Related source pages:** [p100 C](100.md#source-p100-c), [p137 D](137.md#source-p137-d), [p142 A](142.md#source-p142-a).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-radio-contact-operating-times-and-an-unavailable-key"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four independent records describe a broken wire connection, timed
radio calls, an embassy receiving station and the local absence of an
`OSKACHI` key. They use unchanged previously published keys and complete
source frames. They are grouped by subject, not asserted to be one exchange.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [collected intercepts](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and
[certificates](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain exact source rows, headers, key provenance, image hashes, raw readings
and all local repairs. Printed page numbers are three less than PDF page numbers.

<a id="source-p150-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p150-a2-receiving-station-in-the-embassy"></a>

### p150 A2: receiving station in the embassy

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p150_A2.png)
explicitly labels this **part 2**. Its first part has not been attached or
reconstructed in this edition:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (8.55 p.m., November 7th)
PERA OSMAINE 6/11
FUER EILKESE ZU SS D (5) 2200
2 TL RICHI-180
UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN
```

</details>

The page heading is 6 November. The literal `OSMAINE` and `EILKESE` spellings
and the 7 November reception remain unchanged. The instruction separator
before `UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN` is outside the ciphertext.

The 180-slot source contains one dash and gives 89 fixed labels out of 90
under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPEGSSTMTXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADT?SSENCHIFFRITENXINMLLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

Six known-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPFGSSTATXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADRESSENCHIFFRIRENXINALLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

The receiving station (`EMPFGSSTAT`) in the embassy listens for the
recipient. The message supplies the literal name/separator field
`NAMEXQZXX`, asks for addresses to be enciphered, and says to call in every
period. **The precise name boundary within `QZXX` is left unresolved.**
`CHIFFRIREN` and `PERIDEN` remain literal spellings; no extra plaintext
letters are claimed. The opening `JEDOCH` is retained rather than inventing
the missing preceding clause.

Known-coordinate changes, all at zero-based source indices:
**23 X→V, 80 X→V, 86 F→A, 92 X→V, 150 A→V, 167 X→V**.
The separate printed-dash fill is **112 ?→A**. Two of those substitutions
jointly change one raw `E` to `F` in `EMPFGSSTAT`; the certificate does not
collapse their cost into a single coordinate repair.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-verify-and-prior-credit"></a>

### Verify and prior credit

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The independent standard-library verifier rebuilds every source witness,
checks raw domains and numerical fields, and prices substitutions separately
from source-dash fills. No source coordinate is inserted or removed and no
published square is changed. Re-encryption confirms this stated arithmetic,
not the unique history of a damaged word or the identities of station names.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit examples of these bodies; it does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority.

### p100 C: direct contact while the wire is broken

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_C.png)
is under a 1 November heading, with this 2 November reception line:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) UKS v ZÖN (2.03 a.m., November 2nd)
2235 (1) AN LP
RIZI-158
```

</details>

All 158 coordinates give 79 fixed plaintext labels under `Nov1-3`, without
any repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WANNISTUNMITTELBARERVERKEHRMITEUCHXMUENCHENODERBRSLAUMEGLICHXDRAHTUNTERBROCHENX
```

</details>

The sender asks when direct communication with the recipient, Munich or
the place written `BRSLAU` will be possible, and says the wire connection
is interrupted. `BRSLAU` is naturally read as Breslau and `MEGLICH` as a
damaged spelling of *möglich*, but **both remain literal in the certificate**.
No missing plaintext letters are inserted. The separately printed
[p100 B](100.md#edition-cases-military-budapest-wire-break) gives a longer wire-break report;
this does not by itself prove a single transmission or a specific route.

This is distinct from the [p100 challenge](100.md#edition-cases-p100), whose earlier
Belgrade body remains credited to Armin.

### p137 D: the OSKACHI key is no longer here

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p137_D.png)
has `RIZI-102`. Its upper sender initial is overprinted, so the header is
conservatively retained as:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
D) ?CO V OSM (1.55 November 5th,)
RIZI-102
NF NRO V OSM
```

</details>

The page heading is 6 November. Neither it nor the footer is used to resolve
the unclear upper callsign or the time's missing a.m./p.m. designation.
The two dots after the final cipher group `AX` are punctuation; the footer
is outside the 102-coordinate body.

All 51 raw plaintext positions are fixed under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
POTSAGENDA3SSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution, source **79: G→X**, changes the `3`
inside `DA3S` to `S`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
POTSAGENDASSSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> POT sagen, dass Schlüssel OSKACHI hier nicht mehr vorhanden.

It asks that POT be told the `OSKACHI` key is no longer available here.
The key name itself is unchanged. The message does **not** say why it is
unavailable, identify a specific square or rank order, give its operating
period, or connect it to a separate challenge ciphertext. Its presence
inside a telegram decoded with `Nov4-6` does not make `OSKACHI` another name
for that transport key.

The raw numeral `3` remains visible in the original reading and numerical
ledger. Its local word repair does not reassign the square's digit `3`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p142-a-0430-calling-signal-then-listen-again-at-0645"></a>

### p142 A: 0430 calling signal, then listen again at 0645

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_A.png)
is headed 6 November:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) NKJ ZÖN v LP (08.25 p.m., November 6th)
FUER ZÖN 1900 (6/11)
RIZI-128
```

</details>

All 128 coordinates and 64 plaintext labels are fixed under `Nov4-6`, with
no substitutions or fills:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GEBENSIEX0430X10XMINXVVVXDANNIHREFKSPRUNDHOERENSIEUNSWIEDERX0645
```

</details>

The instruction is to send **10 minutes of `VVV` at 0430**, then the
recipient's radiograms (`FKSPR`), and listen again at **0645**. All three
numerical fields are literal published-square readings. No extra day or
time zone is inferred from the evening reception time.

</details>

**Sources on this page:** p150 B1, p150 B2, p150 B3, p150 B4, p150 B5.

<a id="edition-cases-military-wallachia-withdrawal-preparations-wallachia-withdrawal-preparations-p150-b1b5"></a>



**Status:** Five readable parts in their unchanged native source frames. The edition resolves ordinary text while leaving one wholly erased date symbol open.

Source edition and exact verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged **Nov4–6** period key is credited to Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier unreviewed candidates already exposed the first and final parts; their texts and any appearances in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus are retained in the package. The newly complete source edition does not claim first decipherment of every included sentence.

<a id="edition-cases-military-wallachia-withdrawal-preparations-meaning-and-source"></a>

### Meaning and source

The message reports to OHL that OKM has prepared to depart on the raw date `12.11` if ordered. Further delay is considered highly undesirable because of the enemy situation along the Danube, particularly near Rustschuk. If the enemy crosses earlier, the Wallachian plain would have to be evacuated. Advance parties have been sent to Kronstadt and Hermannstadt; railway lines are to come under German operation. Constanta and Medgidia have been evacuated, and the former Dobrudscha administration has moved to Kronstadt as an army rear-area administration.

These are claims in the telegram, not independent verification of the movements. The source's `KONSTANTA` spelling is retained, as are its abbreviations and reference labels.

Childs printed page 150 / PDF page 153 has the page heading 6 November 1918 and intercept header `B) LP v NKJ (--- November 7th)`, `2100 (6) VON UKS 5 TLE`. Those two dates are preserved separately. Parts 1/2/3/5 carry lengths 194/198/204/214. Part 4's length heading is partly cancelled or overwritten; its **202 actual source slots are counted independently**, without reading that number back into the damaged annotation.

<a id="edition-cases-military-wallachia-withdrawal-preparations-exact-boundaries-and-unresolved-date"></a>

### Exact boundaries and unresolved date

The five native plaintext frames join at meaningful word or sentence boundaries: `AEUSSERST / UNERWUENSCHT`, `VORKOMMANDOS / SIND`, and `KONSTANTA U / MEDGIDIA`. Nothing is inserted to connect them.

Part 3's `WALACHEI??E?E` is completed lexically as `WALACHEIEBENE`. The three proposed symbols E/B/N are each allowed by their original observed half-pairs and cost three printed-erasure fills, with no known-coordinate change at those positions. This source-compatible proposal is not a uniqueness proof.

The missing first symbol of `VOR?2X11` has both source coordinates erased, at indices 123 and 183. Its exact domain is all 36 plaintext symbols. The earlier `12X11` field makes a matching date a plausible contextual reading but does not independently recover these two missing coordinates; both remain unfilled. No new numeral mapping is introduced.

The part 4 crop preserves the overlapping typed rows for direct inspection. Every other source frame also retains its original glyph rows and erasure marks.

<a id="edition-cases-military-wallachia-withdrawal-preparations-reproduction-and-attribution-limits"></a>

### Reproduction and attribution limits

There are **zero added or deleted coordinates, block reorders, baseline key changes or new numeral assignments**. Every printed erasure, observed substitution and remaining plaintext domain is recorded in [the certificate](../../experiments/wallachia_withdrawal_preparations/certificates.json), alongside raw and edited round trips. Global completion witnesses are consistency examples, not recovered originals.

The [input record](../../experiments/wallachia_withdrawal_preparations/inputs.json) contains the literal manual rows, original headers and full crop-rendering provenance. The [experiment README](../../experiments/wallachia_withdrawal_preparations/README.md) gives the default verification and optional exact PDF-pixel comparison commands.

A bounded check of the author paper and the cached complete2017 discussion found no explicit prior body identification for these particular records. Earlier machine-derived body leads remain credited, and this check is not a universal priority search.
